theorem-1-1.note: Both conclusions are proved: minimality of the essential norm and uniqueness of the complete algebra norm. The statement includes finite as well as infinite K.

theorem-1-3.note: Proved for arbitrary ordinals over the real or complex field. Continuity is a conclusion; neither the homomorphism nor the Banach algebra is assumed unital.

corollary-1-4.note: Both the operator algebra and the Calkin algebra are covered. The competing algebra norm need not be complete. Uniqueness means equivalence of norms.

theorem-1-5.note: Bonsall minimality is proved for the dual essential norm: every algebra norm dominated by it agrees with it.

theorem-1-6.note: The strict bound and both alternatives for X are proved. No additional factorisation or representation hypothesis remains.

theorem-1-7.note: The exact supremum formula is proved for both alternatives for X. IsLUB expresses the least-upper-bound property, without assuming the supremum is attained.

theorem-3-1.label: factorizationFromDisjointFunctions
theorem-3-1.note: The proved consequence used here starts with disjoint unit-ball functions and a strict uniform lower bound. It gives the required factorisation for either alternative for X. The full equivalence for an arbitrary sequence satisfying the pointwise sum bound is not a theorem in this project.

theorem-3-3.note: The normalized disjoint-function theorem is proved from the scattered, locally compact Hausdorff hypotheses. DisjointFunctionsHalf spells out the norm-one normalization and the interval 0 < δ < 1/2.

lemma-4-5.note: For any finite family of distinct points, the proof constructs pairwise disjoint compact clopen neighbourhoods. This is the stronger form used throughout Sections 4–6.

definition-4-2.note: This finite, indexed structure includes compact clopen neighbourhoods and pairwise disjointness, combining Definitions 4.1–4.2 with the convention in Section 4.

definition-4-6.note: The finite-rank operator is the sum of the point evaluations multiplied by the corresponding compact clopen indicators. Its projection and norm properties are proved in Lemma 4.7.

lemma-4-7.note: All three clauses are proved. The norm-one assertion has the necessary nonempty-family hypothesis; the estimate for I − P holds for every finite family.

proofs.label: (b) Norm one for a nonempty family

theorem-4-8.note: The isometric dual representation is proved over either scalar field, with point masses identified with evaluation functionals. The proof treats locally compact K directly.

definition-4-10.note: Restriction is defined in the atomic representation of the dual: retain the coordinates in C and set the others to zero. Rudin.lean proves that this representation exists.

lemma-4-11.note: The restriction identity and norm additivity are proved for two disjoint sets, giving the finite version by iteration. The general operator estimate recorded here is ≤ 1. Equality requires a nonempty union; it does not hold for the empty restriction.

proposition-5-2.note: The finite-atom construction is proved in atomic coordinates. Its representation hypothesis is established by exists_atomicDualModel; the displayed threshold is the Section 5 bound.

lemma-5-4.note: The essential-weight argument is proved for a bounded operator into ℓ¹(K). Substituting the atomic form of T* gives the paper’s statement.

corollary-5-5.note: Both the subsequence selection in atomic coordinates and its application to T* are proved.

lemma-6-1.note: The infinite diagonal selection is proved in atomic coordinates, from pairwise disjoint finite pieces of sufficiently large mass. The chosen neighbourhoods are disjoint across all stages.

proposition-7-1.note: The dual finite-piece construction is proved for every threshold below ‖T*‖ₑ. The atomic representation appearing in the statement is proved in Rudin.lean.

lemma-8-1.note: The norm-one complemented copy of c₀ is proved for infinite K. That hypothesis is necessary: finite K gives a finite-dimensional C₀(K). The main theorems handle finite K separately.

lemma-8-2.note: The simultaneous factorisation is proved for an orthogonal c₀ block family and the individual factorisation theorem. The completed main proof constructs that family from the complemented c₀ copy and proves the individual factorisations. Choosing ρₙ = 2⁻ⁿ gives the paper’s thresholds.

theorem-3-2.label: dualNormalizedBlockNull_of_not_containsEllOne
theorem-3-2.note: The formal argument proves the normalized weak* null block consequence needed when X contains no copy of ℓ¹. This is the part used in the factorisation proof; the cited closed-subspace formulation is not separately stated.

proposition-9-1.label: continuous_matrix_hom_of_corners
proposition-9-1.note: The substantive forward implication is proved by the diagonal-corner argument for every finite matrix algebra. The reverse implication in the paper follows by taking n = 1; it is not packaged as a separate equivalence.

corollary-9-2.label: continuous_operator_hom_of_finitePower
corollary-9-2.note: The finite-power transfer used in Section 9 is proved at the level of automatic continuity. This declaration is not the paper’s norm-maximality equivalence itself.

theorem-9-3.label: ordinalSpaceReduction
theorem-9-3.note: The project proves the classification consequence needed for Theorem 1.3: the space is finite-dimensional, isomorphic to its square, or isomorphic to a positive finite power of the space on a regular uncountable initial ordinal. The full two-way classification printed here is not formalised.

question-1-2.note: This is a question posed by the paper. The project does not claim an answer.

theorem-1-10.note: Pełczyński’s theorem is quoted as background. Its full non-weak-compactness equivalence is not formalised in this JLMS project; the six main results are proved without using it as an axiom.

remark-1-8.note: This describes an alternative route through a cited duality theorem. The completed proof of Theorem 1.6 uses the direct disjoint-function construction instead.

remark-1-9.note: The sharpness examples in this remark are not separately formalised. The factor-two upper bound itself is proved in Theorem 1.6.

remark-1-11.note: This discusses a proposed extension and work elsewhere. No formal theorem for this discussion is recorded in this project.

definition-4-1.note: Pairwise disjointness is expressed by Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (U i) (U j)). For sets, Disjoint means that their intersection is empty. The fields of NeighborhoodFamily use this condition.

definition-4-3.note: The support of an indexed neighbourhood family U is written ⋃ i, U.sets i. This union is used directly in the essential-weight and diagonal-selection statements; there is no separate named definition.

definition-4-4.note: Finite subsets are represented by Finset K. Countability of a subset A is expressed by A.Countable. These are existing notions in Lean’s libraries, rather than new definitions of this paper.

definition-4-9.note: In atomic coordinates, the support of μ is Function.support (M.representation μ). The representation theorem identifies these coefficients with point masses; atomicDual_countable_support proves the support is countable.

definition-5-1.note: Function.support η denotes {k | η k ≠ 0}; its complement is the zero set. Vanishing on F is written as a pointwise condition ∀ k ∈ F, η k = 0. The constructions use these expressions directly.

remark-5-3.note: The bound ‖I − P‖ ≤ 2 is proved in norm_id_sub_neighborhoodProjection_le_two, linked under Lemma 4.7. It accounts for the threshold δ < 1/2.

remark-7-2.note: The coordinate restriction onto a complement has norm at most one, as proved in norm_id_sub_restrictionL1_le. This is the estimate used by the dual argument. Equality needs a nonempty complement.

remark-8-3.note: Parts of the argument are developed for general factor spaces, but the entire Schauder-decomposition generalisation and all its examples are not recorded as a theorem in this project.

remark-8-4.note: This places the result among related work on uniform incompressibility. The main minimality theorems are formalised; the bibliographical discussion is not a separate Lean theorem.

corollary-7-3.label: theorem_1_7
corollary-7-3.note: The sharp supremum theorem gives this epsilon estimate by choosing a factorisation value sufficiently close to ‖T*‖ₑ. The project’s general result is stated as Theorem 1.7; the separately named epsilon lemma treats the C₀(K) endomorphism case.
